items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma thm:isprop-isprop at source lines 334-336: for every type A the types of proofs that A is a mere proposition and that A is a set are mere propositions. The author's proof (source lines 337-346) has to extract level information from a witness that is only available hypothetically, and it does so twice at different levels. To compare two mere-proposition witnesses it applies function extensionality and then notices that the two values f(x,y) and g(x,y) are paths in A between the same endpoints, equal only because either witness already makes A a mere proposition, hence a set by the preceding result (source lines 338-341). The second half repeats the same manoeuvre for witnesses of sethood, which are functions of four arguments landing in an identity type (source lines 342-345). The statement does not show that equality of the two witnesses is obtained by first turning one of them into a level bound for A.
